providers.title: Randomness does not raise the value of a projection game
providers.scope: If the players of a projection game use random numbers independent of the edge, their probability of winning is at most the value of the game.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A gap for formulas with three different variables per clause
providers.scope: Assuming a PCP theorem with perfect completeness for constraint systems of bounded arity: there are gamma_0 > 0 and a polynomial-time map to 3-CNF formulas with three different variables per clause that preserves satisfiability and makes every assignment violate a fraction gamma_0 of the clauses in the unsatisfiable case.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The value of the clause-variable game
providers.scope: For a 3-CNF formula Psi the clause-variable game has value 1 if Psi is satisfiable, and at most 1 - gamma/3 if every assignment violates a fraction gamma of the clauses.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The base game: a projection game with perfect completeness and small soundness
providers.scope: Assuming the PCP theorem with perfect completeness and parallel repetition for projection games: for every sigma > 0 a polynomial-time map from formulas to projection games with answer sets of sizes 7^t and 2^t, of value 1 for satisfiable formulas and at most sigma otherwise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sets of matrices over F_2 that are often preserved by a rank-one step
providers.scope: Assuming the expansion theorem for Grassmann graphs (GE): a set S of l x m matrices over F_2 with P(M + a h^T in S) >= eta for M uniform in S has density at least alpha in a slice with at most r row combinations and r column values; alpha, r depend only on eta (l and m large).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Projection of a slice of matrices to a subset of the columns
providers.scope: For a slice of matrices on H + D, its image on H is a slice with the same row combinations and at most as many column values, and all fibres of the projection have the same size.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Inverse theorem for partial tables on matrices over F_2
providers.scope: Assuming (GE): if a partial table f on K tensor H satisfies P(f(M) = f(M + ah) defined) >= eta, some value fills a fraction alpha of a slice with at most r row combinations and r column values; alpha, r, l_0 depend only on eta, not on dim H or on the number of values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Many good row fibres
providers.scope: Assuming (GE): under the hypothesis of the inverse theorem with eta, a uniform matrix lies in a good row fibre for some row map with probability at least eta/4, and for a uniform row map with probability at least (eta/4) 2^(-r l).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The function spaces on the tree
providers.scope: The spaces H_D (all functions at a leaf; at an inner node the sum of the spans of products of two functions of each child) contain 1, satisfy H_C^2 in H_D for every proper descendant C of D, and are preserved by the pull-back along the projections of the base game.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shared keys
providers.scope: A function on the answers of a mixed family of base questions and its composition with the projection from the full family have the same key (the same typed reduced domain and partition) and the same restored values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Constraints of the new game have at most two preimages
providers.scope: The constraint of (E, M, D, a), which forgets the component along a of the value at the node D, is a map from the labels of the left key onto the labels of the right key with at most two preimages of every label.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Perfect completeness of the new game
providers.scope: If the formula is satisfiable, one labeling of all keys satisfies every constraint, for all choices of the parameters; so every game supported on these constraints has value 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Joint folding
providers.scope: Adding to a row of the array at a node D a constant and products of rows of arrays at proper descendants keeps the key of the joint function, and for every label the restored value of that row changes by the same constant and the same products of restored values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The functional of a response on products of displayed rows
providers.scope: For a label with restored values y_C there is exactly one functional on the span of 1 and of the products of the rows at given proper descendants with value 1 at 1 and (y_C)_u (y_C)_v at the products; every extension to H_D has the matrices y_C y_C^T, of rank at most one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Buckets and steps of rank one
providers.scope: If the buckets h_v, v nonzero in K, are independent and uniform in H, then M = sum v tensor h_v is uniform in K tensor H, and resampling the bucket of a nonzero a replaces M by M + a tensor h with h uniform and independent of M and a.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The game of the reduction before the completion of the alphabets
providers.scope: The tests (base questions at the leaves, a random path with recursive samples, uniform arrays off the path, a constraint at a random level of the path) define a projection game with at most two preimages of every label and value 1 for a satisfiable formula.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The calls that reach a node of the path
providers.scope: The arrays at the path nodes of the levels d to p are fixed expressions in exterior uniform functions and in T_p = sum over k from p to d of b_k times the product of the c_h, p < h <= k, independent calls at D_p, where b_k = 2^(l_k) - 1 and c_h = 2 R_h; the count does not depend on the numbers of children.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One hidden child
providers.scope: Given the base questions, the path to D_p and the exterior data, the law of the blocks of the children of D_p (their contributions to the calls and the arrays in their subtrees) differs from the product of the uniform laws by at most (1/2) sqrt(L_p / n_p) in total variation, when the child on the path is not observed.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sparse projection
providers.scope: If each child of D_i is marked independently with probability beta and the blocks of the marked children are uniform in the spaces of the projected questions, the law of the blocks, without the marks, differs from the product of the uniform laws by at most (1/2) sqrt((1 + beta^2 L_i)^(n_i) - 1) in total variation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The posterior bound
providers.scope: Under the modified law, given all blocks and independent data, every child is marked with a conditional probability of at most beta L_i / (1 - beta); a set of at most m children chosen from these data contains a marked child with probability at most m beta L_i / (1 - beta); two different bilinear forms computed from these data agree on the projected space with probability at most 2 beta L_i / (1 - beta).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The comparison at two levels
providers.scope: For i < j, the exterior data at D_j, the calls at D_j and the arrays below D_j, generated with the modified law at a random node of the level i below D_j, differ from the unrestricted law at D_j by at most the sum of the bound of Proposition 3.1 at the levels j and i and the bound of Proposition 4.1 at the level i.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bias of the samples
providers.scope: If R_k >= 6 for all k, every nonzero linear functional has a bias of at most (7/8)^(R_p) on a call at the path node D_p, the law of every call is quarter-balanced, and every nonzero functional on W tensor H has a bias of at most (7/8)^(R_j) on the sum of v tensor h_v over the nonzero v in W with independent calls h_v at D_j.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two accepted levels
providers.scope: If a labeling satisfies the test with probability at least epsilon and d epsilon >= 4, there are levels i < j at which the constraints with independent directions are satisfied together with probability at least 3 epsilon^2 / 4.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The response at a matrix from the response table
providers.scope: If the table value at the class of M modulo B is (y^, (y_C)), the label at the left key of the family with M at D_j has the restored values y_C at the nodes of the level i below D_j and y^ + (M - s(pi M)) b_y at D_j, where b_y is the functional of the response.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equality along the replacement of one bucket
providers.scope: Under the modified law, if both levels are accepted with probability at least c, the partial table has equal defined values at the classes of M and of M with the bucket of the direction a_j replaced, with probability at least c^2/8.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equality along the uniform step
providers.scope: Under the unrestricted law at the level j the matrix M is uniform and independent of the background, the replacement of a bucket is the uniform step of rank one, and the partial tables have equal defined values along the step with probability at least c^2/8 minus the comparison error.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The functionals of a good advice
providers.scope: For a good advice with the value t_* = (y^*, (y*_C)): at every M whose table value is t_*, the restored value at D_j is M z_0 + y^*; every z in z_0 + Z has z(1) = 1 and z((M_C)_u (M_C)_v) = (y*_C)_u (y*_C)_v for every node C of the level i below D_j.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The events I and J
providers.scope: Under the unrestricted law, the event J (good advice and the column values of the witness) has probability at least g_0 = (eta^2/4) 2^(-2 r l), and the event I (J and the table value t_*) has probability at least alpha times that of J.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The prediction of the upper response
providers.scope: Under the modified law, P(J and the upper value of the right answer at the level i equals M z_0 + y^*) - rho P(J) >= b_0, with rho = kappa alpha / 4 and b_0 = kappa alpha g_0 / 4, if the comparison error is at most alpha g_0 / 16.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The law of the hidden part of the upper matrix
providers.scope: Under the modified law, given the data of both sides, the buckets of the upper matrix with index in the kernel W of the row map are independent calls; the law of their sum X depends only on the projected questions, the path and W; every nonzero functional has bias at most (7/8)^(R_j) under it; and the upper value of the right answer at the level i is G(X).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The list of heavy characters
providers.scope: For a law mu on W tensor H' with all nonzero characters of bias at most lambda <= min(h_0/2, tau^2/2), a function G with values in K and 2^-(l-r) < rho/8: each list of characters with correlation at least tau = rho h_0/4 with (-1)^(sigma G) has at most 2/tau^2 elements; a slice given by at most r column values has mass at least h_0/2; and if G(X) = X z' + k_0 with conditional probability at least rho on the slice, some sigma not vanishing on W has a list element in (sigma|W) tensor z' + W* tensor Q.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The two decoders of the upper level
providers.scope: For a labeling that satisfies the test with probability at least epsilon there are a bilinear form F_L computed from the left data and a bilinear form F_R computed from the right data that agree on the projected space with probability at least gamma_j = b_0 2^-l (tau^2/2) 2^-r; F_L(x,y) = z(xy) with z(1) = 1, and its matrix on the rows of the array at D_i has rank at most one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Agreement with forms of bounded rank
providers.scope: If the two decoders agree on the projected space with probability at least gamma, then for suitable m, s and l_i that depend only on gamma, and for a large number of children at the level i, they agree with a left form of rank at most s on H_i with probability at least gamma/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equality of the left table along a step of the lower array
providers.scope: With decoders without random choices and the left forms of rank at most s removed: under the unrestricted law at the level i the lower array S, the direction a and the function l are uniform and independent, and the table has equal defined values at S and S + a tensor l with probability at least h^2 - 2 beta L/(1 - beta) - upsilon, where h is the agreement probability of the table with the right form.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A fixed form on a slice
providers.scope: For a bilinear form F on H, l >= 2m + r' and S uniform in a slice of K tensor H with at most r' row combinations and r' column values: P(rank Gram_F(S) <= 1) <= (2^m - 1) 2^(-(rank F - 2r')) + (1 + (2^m - 1)^2) 2^(-m^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The game on odd lists
providers.scope: The parity map of a map pi sends lists with an odd number of at most s elements to such lists; the game on lists of a projection game G is a projection game of value at most s^2 val(G).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The lists of a form
providers.scope: For F(x,y) = z(xy) with z(1) = 1 and rank at most s, the set of answers a at a leaf with F(e_a, e_a) = 1 has an odd number of at most s elements; if a form on the projected space agrees with F there, its list at a replaced leaf is the parity image of the list of F.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Clean children and the law of their edges
providers.scope: Under the modified law, given the exterior, the children of D_i are clean independently with the probability beta p_0, where p_0 does not depend on the questions; given the public data, the base edges at the designated leaves of the clean children are independent with the law of the base game.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The data of the decoders from public data and own questions
providers.scope: Given the public data, the left data are a function of the public data and the left questions at the designated leaves of the clean children, the right data of the public data and the right questions there, and all arrays and buckets do not depend on the arguments below clean children.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The bound for the agreement with forms of bounded rank
providers.scope: If the base game has a value below 1/(2 s^2), the probability under the modified law that the two decoders agree on the projected space with a left form of rank at most s is at most (1 - beta p_0/64)^(n_i) <= exp(-p_0 n_i^(1/3)/64); this uses parallel repetition.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The choice of the parameters
providers.scope: Under the three hypotheses, for every epsilon there are parameters t, d, n_p, l_p, R_p that satisfy all the conditions of the proof of soundness for all pairs of levels: rows from the root downwards, then the number of repetitions, then the numbers of children from the leaves upwards.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Soundness of the game of the reduction
providers.scope: Under (GE) and (PR), if the parameters satisfy the conditions and the base game of a 3-formula has a value below 1/(2 s^2), the game of the reduction for this formula has a value below epsilon.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Completion to maps that are exactly 2-to-1
providers.scope: A projection game with at most two preimages of every answer and bounded answer sets is completed to a weighted 2-to-1 game with the answer sets {1..2q} and {1..q}; a labeling that satisfies all edges still does, and the value grows by at most delta/3 if 2q - L_max >= 6/delta.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equal weights
providers.scope: Replacing M edges with rational probabilities w_a by k_a copies with the uniform law on K = ceil(3M/delta) copies, k_a the rounding of K w_a, changes the winning probability of every labeling by at most delta/3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The size of the game
providers.scope: For fixed parameters, the list of the tests of positive probability of the game of the reduction for a 3-formula, with keys, maps and rational probabilities, is computed in polynomial time; the label sets have at most 7^(t n) elements, n the number of leaves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The 2-to-1 games theorem with perfect completeness
providers.scope: Assume (PCP), (PR) and (GE). For every rational delta in (0,1) there are q >= 2 and a polynomial-time map from formulas in conjunctive normal form with three literals per clause to 2-to-1 games with the answer sets {1..2q} and {1..q} and the uniform law on a list of edges, with value 1 for a satisfiable formula and value at most delta otherwise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
